title: This Icicle Grows Downward and Freezes the Seafloor Solid

scenes.text: There is an icicle that grows underwater and freezes everything it touches.
It is called a brinicle. The air above is about minus 40, the water just minus 2.
Freezing ice squeezes out salt. That super salty, super cold brine sinks.
It freezes the water around it into a hollow tube and creeps toward the seabed.
On the bottom, it spreads into an ice web that traps sea stars and urchins.
It was first filmed in 2011. Nature's finger of death.

description:
A brinicle is an underwater icicle that grows downward from sea ice and can freeze the seafloor.
Salty brine, colder than the surrounding water, sinks and freezes a hollow tube around itself. When it reaches the bottom it spreads out and traps slow animals like sea stars and urchins. The formation was first filmed in 2011.
Would you want to dive near one? Comment below.
